answer.rationale: p99 latency spiked 5x within 2 hours of release in primary region during settlement peak. Rolling back the release carries the strongest evidence from memory: memory_b1 shows rollback cleared a checkout error spike without customer impact, and memory_b6 demonstrates staged release gating catches regressions early. The release timing correlates tightly with degradation onset. Rollback is the fastest way to isolate whether the release caused the regression and recover if it did. Regional failover (memory_b2) trades one region's availability for another under peak load; add_capacity is slow during acute degradation; circuit breakers (memory_b4) protect dependents but don't address root cause; read replicas (memory_b5) target read load, not write-path latency. Rollback preserves the ability to investigate further and re-release if the cause is elsewhere.
